Gmail and IMAP decode UTF-8, Big5, GB18030 and legacy Japanese mail. Gmail reads quoted MIME charset parameters and RFC2231 continuations. When non-ASCII UTF-8 and the declared charset disagree, Gmail uses one original-MIME read rather than guessing. This exceptional read includes attachment bytes within the 35 MiB message limit, without saving ordinary files. The reader discloses detected decoding loss or an unknown charset without guessing another encoding. The message list shows the same stored subject and snippet as the reader for persisted server mail and does not guess another encoding. The reader automatically shows healthy plain text when HTML decoding lost characters and MIME confirms they are versions of the same content. Independent sections and older cached messages without that confirmation keep their available HTML and encoding warnings. When both versions are available, use Show plain-text version to switch the current reading view. In the Reader, look beside Summary when available. Use Show HTML version to switch back. HTML stays sanitized and remote images keep their existing permission. Download completeness and encoding notices are separate. Older cached replacement characters get an uncertainty notice. Retry download explicitly rechecks the server copy, including complete cached messages, but cannot recover bytes already lost by the sender or provider. Received Gmail messages without a warning also offer Reload message beside Summary for explicitly replacing an older cached body. Failed reloads retain complete cached content; pending drafts are not replaced. No cache-wide repair runs automatically. Encoding diagnostics store fixed flags only, without message contents or telemetry.
